note: The single most instructive ICP case in this batch, because the stated definition names physicians explicitly and this is the only physician in twelve files — and he sits outside the ICP on everything else. Successful: a radiology resident one year from completing training, which is the occupation the criterion describes. Neglected health: the textbook version, a decade of medical school and residency at 80 hours a week with the body left behind. Then it breaks. Income: he called $6,000 'literally impossible', said $3,000 would be too, expected 'a couple hundred dollars', and refused both a credit card and a loan on principle — and the reason is structural, because residents are not paid like attendings, which the stated ICP does not distinguish. Good to great: he has gained roughly 80 lb, guesses 30% body fat and rates his cardiovascular fitness 2 out of 10; this is rescue by any reading. Not deconditioned: he is the excluded profile almost word for word — well over 50 lb above his former weight, describing treadmill cardio as 'torture'. The finding for the rollup is that occupation and income came apart completely here. Screening on job title would have qualified him and screening on capacity to pay would have disqualified him, and the funnel did the former.
